Tamil Nadu Mandates GIS-Based Master Plans for Urban Local Bodies

2026-08-27 Rudhran Baraasu, The New Indian Express Tamil Nadu, GIS, master plans, urban planning, land use, geospatial, urban local bodies, India
Read the source article

Quick summary

The Tamil Nadu government has mandated that all urban local bodies and development authorities prepare, approve, and adopt legally valid GIS-based Master Plans, Zonal Plans, and Land Use Plans using standardised geospatial methodologies.

Key takeaways

  • Tamil Nadu's housing and urban development department issued a Government Order (dated August 11) mandating GIS-based Master Plans across all Urban Local Bodies (ULBs)
  • The state's existing 123 Master Plans, governing 130 towns, were built using conventional methods and lack a digital, data-driven foundation
  • The spatial database will include administrative boundaries, cadastral parcels, transportation networks, land use, building footprints, water bodies, utilities, and demographic data
  • All planning bodies must follow a rigid digital framework from baseline benchmarking to final proposal formulation
  • Approved GIS-based plans must be uploaded online for transparency and inter-departmental use
